History:
- Chief complaint: Swelling over the left elbow noticed ~1 week ago.
- Course: Non-painful; slightly warm; feels fluid-filled. Able to move elbow normally. Mild tenderness adjacent to the swelling; tip of elbow not tender.
- Context: No known trauma or injury. Desk-based job. No prior similar episodes reported.
- Associated symptoms: None documented (no systemic symptoms discussed).

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP a few years ago).
- Allergies: Peanuts.
- Medication allergies: None known.
- Medications: None routinely.
- Social: Runs 2–3 times/week; desk job.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth video inspection of left elbow:
  - Visible localized swelling.
  - Patient-reported warmth compared to surrounding skin.
  - Mild tenderness adjacent to swelling; tip of olecranon non-tender on self-palpation.
  - Full range of motion preserved per patient.
  - Dry skin noted over tip of elbow.
  - Redness not documented.

Impression:
- Likely left olecranon bursitis; low clinical concern for septic arthritis at present. Workup planned to rule out inflammatory, infectious, or crystal arthropathy (including gout).

Management Plan:
- Medication: Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily; route not documented. Take after food; stop if heartburn occurs. Over-the-counter.
- Investigations: Blood tests to be arranged via mailed forms—check inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout screen.
- Results/Timing: Results expected ~5–6 days after blood draw (mailing time for forms may add delay).
- Follow-up: Arrange review (video/phone or in-person) after labs to reassess the elbow and review results.
- Safety net: Seek urgent assessment if the elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads (possible emergency).

Patient Summary:
- 53-year-old man with a 1-week history of painless, warm swelling over the left elbow and preserved motion. Exam consistent with olecranon bursitis; no current features suggestive of septic arthritis. NSAID started; blood tests ordered to evaluate for inflammatory/infectious causes including gout; follow-up arranged after results.

Key Takeaways:
- Take ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; stop if heartburn occurs.
- Complete the mailed blood tests promptly and contact the clinic to schedule follow-up.
- Seek urgent care if redness becomes pronounced, pain becomes severe, or redness spreads.

Next Steps:
- Complete ordered blood tests upon receipt of forms; expect results ~5–6 days after sampling.
- Book follow-up (telemedicine or in-person) to review results and reassess the elbow.
- Request earlier in-person review if symptoms worsen.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals; fever/chills and other systemic review.
  - Exact description of erythema, size of swelling, neurovascular status, skin breaks, ROM quantification.
  - Past history of gout, recent infections, repetitive pressure/trauma, diabetes/immunosuppression, tobacco/alcohol history.
  - Immunizations, prior surgeries/hospitalizations, imaging, or aspiration discussion.
● Internal conflicts:
  - None noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Some sections were partially inaudible/ellipses, but key clinical details and plan were clear.
